input_signals.hypothesis: Capital raised and immediately consumed — external funding that does not show up as an increase in the cash balance — is qualitatively worse than capital raised and held, and worst of all when the absorbing use is a swelling working-capital position rather than productive investment.
input_signals.reasoning: Every prior financing leg measured the *amount* raised, which is why FF5's investment factor absorbed it; this leg measures the *fate* of the money (raised minus retained in cash), a disposition variable that is not a scaled investment characteristic and therefore has a better chance of surviving the CMA control. Conjoining it with the working-capital accrual identifies firms whose new outside money went into receivables and inventory — the classic soft-asset buildup that later reverses.

input_signals.reasoning: This is not an average of previously tested legs with arbitrary weights but a single accounting share in which accruals and financing are inseparable: the same dollar of accrual simultaneously reduces cash-backed earnings in the denominator and raises the external share, so the numerator and denominator cannot be decomposed into the archive's two legs. Being a bounded proportion rather than an unbounded stress ratio, it is well behaved as a Fama-MacBeth regressor — addressing the family's chronic null slope — while remaining distinct from a scaled investment characteristic because two firms with identical asset growth score very differently depending on the cash content of their earnings.
